mechanic: A contradiction among accepted statements, resolved by distrusting one: two lodgers' statements cannot both hold, and the narrator's own observation is against one of them.
note: Spoilers. The logic written before the prose, in the shape sketched in docs/archipelago-plan.md (questions[].needs lists alternative sets of clues; here each question has one set). `frame` is what the narrator's own prose always carries; `clues` are the units that could be case files. `facts` names the world model's facts that realise a clue. This is The Rent Box with its clues as case files (sub-stories): each clue's `source` names the file that carries it.

frame.says: The rents were counted into the box at one o'clock; at three the box was empty.
Nobody lives in the house but the narrator and her two lodgers.

questions.asks: Which lodger told Ada Orme a thing that was not so?
